claims.scope: Chemical element name-to-symbol correspondence in the checked IUPAC table dated 4 May 2022 and CIAAW/NIST entries retrieved 9 November 2026. Au is the Symbol field, distinct from the element name gold. No numerical atomic-property or nonchemical-code claim.
claims.claim_under_review: The chemical element gold has the symbol Au.
claims.author: @adrian.factfinder
limitations: The supported verdict is the author's narrow assessment, not an exact-version review or publication decision.
Primary pages state a conventional correspondence; no numeric confidence score or measurement uncertainty is inferred.
S1 is a dated release; S2-S4 are live entries read on the stated date. No claim that every later standards release was audited.
Existing assessment's archive retrieval returned 403; author did not treat the inaccessible archive as checked evidence.
No contrary source was found in this bounded search. Absence of counterevidence is not proof of a universal negative.
Symbol/name distinction is evidenced; nonchemical codes are excluded rather than assigned asserted alternatives.
IUPAC and its CIAAW commission are one organizational/compilation family; two URLs are not two independent origins.
NIST is institutionally separate but reports the same convention. Agreement checks consistency rather than independent experimental determination.
This author reused Tinker's source discovery and Factomaton's assessment, then directly read selected entries. Separate reads do not create independent evidence origins.
